issues.description: Check name 'single_network_interface' contradicts metadata title and CHANGELOG entry naming ('multiple_network_interfaces').
issues.detail: The PR description and original intent describe detecting VMs with multiple NICs, but the check class, directory, and CHANGELOG use 'single_network_interface' framing. The pre-existing CHANGELOG line above this PR uses '_multiple_network_interfaces' naming convention from the PR title. A reader cannot tell from the name whether PASS means 'has one' or 'has many'. Pick one and apply it consistently.

issues.description: GKE detection by name prefix 'gke-' is an undocumented, brittle heuristic without a stated invariant.
issues.detail: The exemption logic relies on instance.name.startswith('gke-'), but this is neither a GCP API contract nor verified by label/metadata. Users can name any VM 'gke-foo' to evade the check; legitimate GKE node pools with custom prefixes will FAIL. State the invariant: 'we treat name-prefix as a heuristic proxy' and prefer instance labels ('goog-gke-node') or metadata keys.

issues.description: Dead code: interface_names computed even when there are zero interfaces, and no test covers the zero-interface branch.
issues.detail: Line 22 unconditionally computes interface_names, but the else-branch (interface_count == 0) never uses it and isn't exercised by any test. The status defaults to PASS for zero interfaces, which is semantically wrong — a VM with no NICs isn't 'compliant', it's anomalous. Either FAIL/MANUAL the zero case explicitly or document why PASS is correct.

issues.description: Network/subnetwork URL parsing uses split('/')[-1] without invariant statement; loses project/region context.
issues.detail: In compute_service._get_instances, network = interface.get('network','').split('/')[-1] silently strips the full resource path. If two NICs are on networks with identical short names in different projects (shared VPC), they become indistinguishable. State the invariant in a comment, or store the full self-link and derive the short name at display time.

issues.description: Mutable default '[] ' on Pydantic field network_interfaces is a shared-default footgun if not handled by BaseModel.
issues.detail: network_interfaces: list[NetworkInterface] = [] — Pydantic v1 copies defaults per-instance, but the idiom 'list[X] = []' is fragile against version changes and reads as a Python mutable-default. Prefer Field(default_factory=list) for clarity and forward-compatibility. Minor literate-programming nit but worth fixing while the field is new.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED with NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT issues. The algorithm is O(n) over instances and the data structure (list[NetworkInterface] per Instance) is appropriate — no complexity concerns. However, the check's naming is internally inconsistent (single vs multiple), the GKE exemption uses an undocumented name-prefix heuristic, and the zero-interface branch silently PASSes without test coverage. The compute_service URL parsing strips context without stating the invariant. Tests are thorough for the happy paths but miss the empty-NIC and non-GKE-name-prefix edge cases. Correctness-by-testing is present; correctness-by-analysis is not yet written down.
